claim: Blood draws a sprite at its own shade PLUS its sector's: the ceiling shade when the sector is open to the sky (ceilingstat 1) and floorstat bit 0x8000 is clear, otherwise the floor shade (plus SHADE.DAT per-tile terms). An outdoor sprite is lit by the sky shade, not by the ground it stands on.
evidence: Campaign: an open sector's sky shade is its floor shade minus 16 at the median (quartiles -28/-6); floorstat 0x8000 is set in only 12 of 1,768 open sectors (2026-11-20).
Gravesend had every sky shade at 0, so every outdoor sprite was drawn full bright in the game; the owner saw it.

NBlood/source/blood/src/view.cpp:2875-2882 viewProcessSprites is the only read of floorstat 0x8000; the XMapEdit observer draws a sprite's own shade, so until 2026-11-20 frames showed every outdoor sprite lighter or darker than the game (bloodmap/visual.py sprite_shades_as_drawn)
use: Any lighting pass must set sky (ceiling) shades of open sectors as well as floors; a light sprite carries a strongly negative shade of its own (flames -128). Frames from a renderer that draws raw sprite shade lie: bake the rule in. Set floorstat 0x8000 on open sectors so the sky can be one shade and sprites follow the ground (daylight.SPRITES_TAKE_FLOOR).
